checks: Verified 61c2a6c203bcade2 §6 gives the same arc and support ceiling, with the claim about all boundary traces kept separate from finite response coordinates.

The ceiling 1+dist(u,A)² is continuous and majorizes the disk support. At each circle point the unique normal is the point itself, and the cut is active exactly on A. The physical trace is therefore the stated indicator.

Almost-everywhere equality forces the constants on the two neighboring open arcs because every open subarc has positive measure. The two one-sided limits contradict continuity. The finite-penalty trace convergence has the same arc-length measure.

dependencies.hypotheses: Same-batch prerequisite, independently reviewed. Take a singleton base, the disk, continuous support ceiling and constant field 1. Its contact-speed formula and finite-penalty closure apply with ordinary arc length.

overlap.comparison: The radial formula immediately identifies this speed for the supplied action. It does not itself give the no-continuous-trace witness or the L1 approximation by single convex potentials.

readability: A proper nontrivial closed arc has an endpoint with both an interior arc and its open complement adjacent.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the frozen input, original source comparison, predecessor checks, and direct derivation or exact arithmetic replay where applicable.
summary: The disk arc is an actual cut-contact trace with a jump at an endpoint. Continuity cannot realize that trace even almost everywhere, while convex penalty traces converge in arc-length L1.
